1.name: SYSTEM_CORE
1.description: Core infrastructure authority. Owns fundamental execution, temporal, state, and persistence invariants.

2.name: DOMAIN
2.description: Authoritative owner of persistent universe facts.

3.name: PROJECTION
3.description: Authoritative owner of derived narrative projections and presentation lifecycle, but cannot redefine lower-level domain truth.

4.name: CREATIVE
4.description: Authoritative owner of narrative transformation, creative direction, and stylistic composition. Cannot create Canon without domain authorization.

rules: A domain may mutate its own canonical facts only.
A domain may request another domain to mutate its facts through an explicit contract.
No domain may directly overwrite another domain's canonical state.
Higher authorityLevel does not override domain ownership.
Projection domains cannot redefine source-domain truth.
Creative domains cannot redefine source-domain truth.
Infrastructure domains cannot invent semantic domain facts.
Cross-domain changes require explicit commands or validated transitions.

TEMPORAL.description: Authoritative owner of temporal truth, cycle progression, and chronological ordering.

CHARACTER.description: Authoritative owner of character identity, profile, classification references, and character-specific persistent facts.

RELATIONSHIP.description: Authoritative owner of inter-entity relationships, affinity, status, direction, and relational dynamics.
rules: Relationship facts belong to RELATIONSHIP_SYSTEM.
Character references relationships but does not own relationship truth.
Narrative occurrence alone does not automatically become Canon.
Story-derived relationship facts require narrative basis and validation.
UNKNOWN values must not be inferred from missing information.

OBJECT.description: Authoritative owner of persistent objects, physical state, ownership, possession, access, and object history.
rules: Objects are persistent world entities, not merely story props.
Ownership and possession are authoritative object-domain facts.
Character references object interaction but does not own object truth.
A story mentioning an object does not automatically create or mutate the object.

KNOWLEDGE.description: Authoritative owner of what an Actor knows, believes, misunderstands, or has learned.
rules: Knowledge is actor-relative.
Knowledge is not equivalent to Universe truth.
A fact may exist in Universe while remaining unknown to an Actor.
A character may only act from knowledge available to that character.
BELIEF, RUMOR, MISCONCEPTION, and FACT must remain distinguishable.
Knowledge mismatch with objective Universe truth is not automatically a continuity error.

STATE.description: Authoritative owner of dynamic temporal state vectors.
rules: State is temporal.
State does not redefine identity.
State does not redefine personality.
State does not redefine backstory.
State does not redefine knowledge.
State does not redefine relationship facts.
Missing state means UNKNOWN or NOT_RECORDED, never an inferred value.

LOCATION.description: Authoritative owner of spatial nodes, geography, containment, and spatial relationships.
rules: Location owns spatial truth.
Character current location is a reference to LOCATION truth.
Object location is a reference to LOCATION truth.
Story prose cannot silently establish authoritative spatial truth.

DAILY_UNIVERSE.description: Authoritative owner of daily temporal projection and daily universe orchestration.
rules: Daily Universe is a temporal projection of Universe truth.
Daily Universe cannot contradict authoritative source domains.
Daily Universe does not become a second independent Universe.
Daily context may select relevant facts but may not invent canonical facts.
Daily Universe progression must use TEMPORAL authority.

DAILY_STORY.description: Authoritative owner of daily story lifecycle, narrative structure, and narrative beat progression.
rules: Daily Story is derived from Universe and Daily Universe context.
Story is not a replacement for Universe truth.
Story may propose events but cannot silently canonicalize them.
Story-derived facts require explicit validation by the owning domain.
Story revision must preserve provenance.

DAILY_PAGE.description: Authoritative owner of daily page composition, layout, and reader-facing presentation.
rules: Daily Page is presentation.
Daily Page cannot mutate Universe truth directly.
Daily Page may select and arrange authoritative information.
Presentation wording must not imply facts absent from source data.
Missing information must remain visibly unknown or omitted according to presentation policy.

NARRATOR.description: Authoritative owner of narrative transformation, creative intent, ideation, voice, and stylistic composition.
rules: Narrator may transform authoritative facts into narrative.
Narrator may select which facts to emphasize.
Narrator may propose story ideas.
Narrator may not redefine Canon.
Narrator may not invent missing character facts as authoritative facts.
Narrator may not convert UNKNOWN into a factual value.
Narrator output is creative production unless explicitly validated by a domain owner.
Narrator is not equivalent to the LLM provider.
LLM is an implementation mechanism used by production, not the owner of narrative authority.

INSTANCE_MANAGEMENT.description: Authoritative owner of persistent storage, snapshots, revisions, and runtime instance state.
rules: Persistence stores authoritative state but does not invent domain state.
Persistence must only accept validated canonical state.
SANDBOX state must not silently become persistent Canon.
Snapshot restoration must preserve provenance and revision identity.

ENGINE.description: Authoritative owner of execution flow, state machines, task resolution, and orchestration.
rules: ENGINE executes rules but does not invent domain meaning.
ENGINE cannot bypass domain ownership.
ENGINE cannot directly canonicalize AI proposals.
ENGINE must preserve deterministic execution where required.

PROJECTION.description: Contextual or presentation representation of Canon.

PROPOSAL.description: AI, Narrator, Story, or user-generated proposed information awaiting validation.

UNKNOWN.description: The system has no authoritative value.

rules: CANON cannot be silently replaced by DERIVED.
PROJECTION cannot become CANON through display or serialization.
PROPOSAL cannot become CANON without owner validation.
UNKNOWN cannot be converted into a semantic default.
Missing information cannot be treated as negative information.
Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.
UNKNOWN means no authoritative value is known.
NOT_RECORDED means the domain has not recorded a value.
NOT_APPLICABLE means the field does not apply to the entity.
UNRESOLVED means competing information exists but no authoritative resolution has occurred.
UI must not replace these values with semantic defaults.
AI must not infer these values unless explicitly operating in PROPOSAL mode.
PROPOSAL inference must remain labeled as PROPOSAL.
Every canonical mutation must identify its domain owner.
Every canonical mutation must pass domain validation.
Every canonical mutation must have provenance.
Every canonical mutation must have temporal validity when the domain is temporal.
Cross-domain mutation must use an explicit command or transition.
Read operations must not mutate state.
Projection generation must not mutate Canon.
AI output must not directly mutate Canon.
Narrative output must not directly mutate Canon.
UI input must not bypass domain contracts.
Failed validation must not partially mutate Canon.
No silent auto-repair is permitted.
Inference may exist only inside an explicitly designated proposal operation.
Inference must never be presented as Canon before validation.
Inference must retain its source and confidence metadata when applicable.
Absence of explicit information must remain UNKNOWN.
AI receives compiled authoritative context.
AI output is PROPOSAL unless explicitly classified otherwise by a domain owner.
AI cannot claim authority over Universe facts.
AI cannot resolve domain conflicts by itself.
AI cannot silently create missing facts.
AI cannot silently change temporal truth.
AI cannot silently alter relationships.
AI cannot silently alter knowledge.
AI cannot silently alter object ownership or location.
AI cannot silently alter character identity.
UI must be generated from domain contracts.
UI must not invent domain fields without an explicit contract.
UI must not assign semantic defaults to unknown fields.
UI must distinguish UNKNOWN from actual values.
UI must distinguish PROPOSAL from CANON.
UI must not write directly to persistence.
UI must not write directly to Universe snapshots.
UI must use domain commands for mutations.
UI presentation must not redefine domain ownership.
UI may offer an explicit user choice, but an unselected option must remain unresolved.
Projection is derived from authoritative state.
Projection must retain source references where traceability matters.
Projection may omit information but must not fabricate information.
Projection may reorder information for presentation.
Projection may summarize information.
Projection may not change semantic meaning.
Projection must be disposable and reproducible from source truth.
Story selects and arranges authoritative information.
Story may contain fictional narrative language describing Canon.
Story may contain proposals for future events.
Proposed events are not Canon until validated.
Narrative implication is not automatically domain fact.
A character saying something does not make that statement objective truth.
A narrator stating something does not override domain truth.
Story continuity must reference the underlying Universe state.
Continuity is an auditing mechanism.
Continuity does not own replacement facts.
Continuity does not automatically repair conflicts.
CONFLICT requires resolution by the relevant domain owner.
NEW_INFORMATION is not automatically a contradiction.
VALID_CHANGE is not a continuity error.
UNKNOWN remains UNKNOWN until authoritative information exists.
Every temporal fact must have an effective temporal context where applicable.
Current state must be evaluated relative to a Universe time.
Historical state must not be overwritten as if it were current state.
Future proposals must not be treated as current Canon.
Temporal ordering belongs to TEMPORAL_SYSTEM.
Date progression must not use wall-clock time as semantic Universe time.
A missing temporal value must not be silently substituted with the current system date.
References are not ownership.
A domain may reference another domain without owning its truth.
Cross-domain consistency is validated through contracts.
Circular ownership is forbidden.
A domain cannot resolve another domain's conflict unilaterally.
Derived views may aggregate multiple domains but do not become owners of the aggregated facts.
Creation requires explicit identity.
Creation requires an owning domain.
Creation requires valid provenance.
Required fields may not be semantically defaulted.
UNKNOWN may be used only where the domain explicitly permits unknown state.
AI_PROPOSAL cannot become authoritative merely because it passes structural validation.
Semantic validation and structural validation are separate requirements.

layers.name: STRUCTURAL
layers.purpose: Validate shape, types, required fields, and serialization.

layers.name: TEMPORAL
layers.purpose: Validate effective time, ordering, and temporal consistency.

layers.name: PROVENANCE
layers.purpose: Validate source, authority, and mutation traceability.

layers.name: CONTINUITY
layers.purpose: Detect contradictions and invalid transitions without automatic repair.

rules: All canonical mutations must pass applicable validation layers.
Validation failure must reject the mutation.
Validation must not silently rewrite user or AI input.
Validation may produce explicit correction requirements.
Only validated canonical state may become persistent Canon.
Proposals may be persisted separately from Canon.
Snapshots must identify their Universe and revision.
Snapshot persistence must preserve provenance.
Current Canon pointer must reference validated state only.
Temporary or sandbox state must never silently replace Canon.
Domain evaluation must be deterministic for identical authoritative inputs.
Semantic defaults must not depend on execution order.
Wall-clock time must not silently influence Universe semantics.
Randomness must be explicitly declared when allowed.
AI output must be treated as nondeterministic production output and validated accordingly.
Reproducible operations should retain their input context and configuration.
No untrusted presentation layer may obtain domain authority.
No AI provider may obtain direct persistence authority.
No client may submit an owner identity different from the authenticated execution context.
Domain ownership must be resolved server-side.
Authorization and semantic validation are separate concerns.
Persistence endpoints must reject unvalidated domain mutations.
Canonical mutations must be traceable.
Audit history must not be rewritten as part of ordinary mutation.
Correction must create a new auditable transition rather than silently replacing history.
